A lot of child advocacy depends on how your home state. I know in my home state there are attorneys whose main area of practice is Guardian Ad Litem (GAL) work. In my home state GALs for children will often times be appointed in both divorce cases as well as Abuse/Neglect/Dependency cases.

Summer after my 1L year I clerked for my local Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) program. CASA programs are located all over the country and are always looking for volunteers. If you volunteer with your local CASA program it will expose you to the kinds of work GALs do. During my clerkship I helped the attorneys for the program draft motions and do some legal research.

It is possible for you to survive off of a GAL salary. GALs in divorce cases often times can charge more per hour but depending on the case you might be stuck with the "do I stop doing work and piss off the court or do I keep doing work and extend the proceedings till I get paid" dilemma (this is a drastic oversimplification but the idea is there).

Another area where you could look into is Juvenile Justice/Juvenile Defense work. Think public defenders office but the Juvenile division. When you start to consider things like bindovers (sending a juvenile from juvenile court to adult court) and how they effect juveniles it will give you a new perspective on that system.

Hope this helps!
